text: “You must take good care of him, Matt,” Scott said, as they started down the hill. “Write and let me know how he gets along.” “Sure,” the dog-musher answered. “But listen to that, will you!” Both men stopped. White Fang was howling as dogs howl when their masters lie dead. He was voicing an utter woe, his cry bursting upward in great heart-breaking rushes, dying down into quavering misery, and bursting upward again with a rush upon rush of grief.
